title: Islamic Civil Calendar
intro: The Islamic Civil calendar is a deterministic tabular Hijri date system using the Friday epoch.
epoch: 1 Muharram AH 1 corresponds to JDN 1948440 (16 July 622 Julian).
structure: Twelve months alternate 30 and 29 days; the final month, Dhu al-Hijjah, has 30 days in a leap year. The year contains 354 or 355 days.
model: A year is leap when the positive remainder of (11 × year + 14) divided by 30 is below 11. This gives eleven leap years in a 30-year cycle (10631 days). For year y, month m and day d, JDN = epoch - 1 + d + floor((59(m-1)+1)/2) + 354(y-1) + floor((3+11y)/30). Conversion uses checked/validated arithmetic.
example: In year 2 the final month has 30 days; in year 1 it has 29. The civil epoch is one day later than the separate astronomical-epoch tabular provider.
history: Arithmetic tables provide a reproducible chronology for records and calculations; Islamic communities also use observation-based or authority-specific dates.
limits: The rule is not a prediction of crescent visibility or a religious determination. Local observed or historical dates can differ.
